1
自天地剖判，日月運行，剛柔相摩，寒暑交謝，分之以氣序，紀之以星辰，弦望有盈缺，明晦有修短。 古先哲王則之成化，迎日推策，各有司存，以天下之至王，盡生民之能事，先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。 及卯金受命，年曆屢改，當塗啟運，日官變業，分路揚鑣，異門馳騖，回互靡定，交錯不等。 豈是人情淺深，苟相違異？ 蓋亦天道盈縮，欲止不能。
Ever since Heaven and Earth were sundered, the sun and moon have pursued their circuits, yin and yang rubbing against each other as cold and warmth succeed one another. The seasons are ordered by the flow of qi, the heavens marked by the stars; the moon's phases wax and wane, and light and dark each have their measure. The sage rulers of old modeled themselves on these patterns to bring civilization to fulfillment. They greeted the sun and advanced the reckoning, each duty assigned to its officer. As kings paramount under Heaven, they brought all that the people could accomplish to bear—acting before Heaven so that Heaven did not thwart them, and acting after Heaven so that they accorded with its seasons. When the Han dynasty received the Mandate, calendrical systems were revised again and again. When the Wei rose to power, the official astronomers changed their methods. Calendrical schools went their separate ways, each pursuing its own course, so that systems overlapped and conflicted without ever settling into agreement. Surely this was not merely a matter of human prejudice, with scholars capriciously disagreeing? Rather, it reflected the waxing and waning of the Heavenly Way—one might wish to halt the process, but could not.
2
正光之曆既行於世，發元壬子，置差令朔。 [1]測影清臺，懸炭之期或爽； 候氣重室，布灰之應少差。 伏惟陛下當璧膺符，大橫恊兆，乘機虎變，撫運龍飛，苞括九隅，牢籠萬宇，四海來王，百靈受職。 大丞相、勃海王降神挺生，固天縱德，負圖作宰，知機成務，撥亂反正，決江疏河，效顯勤王，勳彰濟世。 功成治定，禮樂惟新，以履端歸餘，術數未盡，乃命兼散騎常侍執讀臣李業興，大丞相府東閤祭酒、夷安縣開國公臣王春，大丞相府戶曹參軍臣和貴興等，委其刊正。 但回舍有疾徐，推步有疏密，不可以一方知，難得以一途揆。 大丞相主簿臣孫搴，驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫臣曄，前給事黃門侍郎臣季景，勃海王世子開府諮議參軍事、定州大中正臣崔暹，業興息國子學生、屯留縣開國子臣子述等，並令參豫，定其是非。
After the Zhengguang calendar came into use, with its epoch set in a renzi year, it adjusted discrepancies to fix the new moons. [1] On the Clear Terrace where shadows were measured, the timing of the suspended-charcoal test sometimes proved off; and in the sealed chamber where seasonal qi was observed, the ash-line responses showed small errors. We humbly observe that Your Majesty has received the Mandate, the great portent aligning with Heaven's signs; rising with the tiger's swift transformation and ascending with the dragon's flight, you encompass the farthest reaches and hold all under Heaven within your grasp, so that the four seas pay homage and the myriad spirits take their appointed places. The Grand Chancellor, Prince of Bohai, was born of Heaven's grace, endowed with virtue by nature. Bearing the cosmic chart as chief minister, he seized the opportune moment and accomplished great tasks—quelling disorder, restoring order, cutting through rivers and opening waterways—his loyalty to the throne and his service to the age shining forth in equal measure. Once success was won and order restored, rites and music were renewed; yet the calendrical reckoning of year-beginnings and intercalary remainders was still incomplete. The Emperor therefore commissioned Li Yexing, Reader-in-Attendance, Wang Chun, Libationer of the Grand Chancellor's Eastern Pavilion and Duke of Yi'an, He Guixing of the Household Section, and others to revise and correct the calendar. Yet the cycles of lodge-return vary in speed, and computational steps differ in density; no single method can grasp the whole, nor can one pathway alone serve to judge them. Sun Qian, Registrar to the Grand Chancellor; Ye, General of Agile Cavalry and Left Household Gentleman of the Luminous Hall; Ji Jing, former Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; Cui Xian, Consultant of the Bohai Heir Apparent's staff and Chief Rectifier of Ding Province; Zi Shu, son of Li Yexing, Imperial University student and Baron of Tunliu—all were ordered to take part and adjudicate the merits of the calendar.
3
臣等職司其憂，猶恐未盡。 竊以蒙戎為飾，必藉眾腋之華； 輪奐成宇，寧止一枝之用。 必集名勝，更共修理。 左光祿大夫臣盧道約，大司農卿、彭城侯臣李諧，左光祿大夫、東雍州大中正臣裴獻伯，散騎常侍、西兗州大中正臣溫子昇，太尉府長史臣陸操，尚書右丞、城陽縣開國子臣盧元明，中書侍郎臣李同軌，前中書侍郎臣邢子明，中書侍郎臣宇文忠之，前司空府長史、建康伯臣元仲悛，大丞相法曹參軍臣杜弼，尚書左中兵郎中、定陽伯臣李溥濟，尚書起部郎中臣辛術，尚書祠部郎中臣元長和，前青州驃騎府司馬、安定子臣胡世榮，太史令、盧鄉縣開國男臣趙洪慶，太史令臣胡法通，應詔左右臣張喆，員外司馬督臣曹魏祖，太史丞郭慶，太史博士臣胡仲和等，或器標民譽，或術兼世業，並能顯微闡幽，表同錄異，詳考古今，共成此曆。 甲為日始，子實天正，命曆置元，宜從此起。 運屬興和，以年號為目，豈獨太初表於漢代，景初冠於魏曆而已。 謹以封呈，乞付有司，依術施用。
We who hold this office bear the responsibility, yet still fear our efforts may fall short. We venture to think that a fur cloak cannot be made from a single patch of hide; nor can a great hall be built from a single rafter alone. Renowned experts must be gathered to revise the work together. Lu Daoyue, Left Household Gentleman of the Luminous Hall; Li Xie, Minister of Grand Agriculture and Marquis of Pengcheng; Pei Xianbo, Left Household Gentleman and Chief Rectifier of Eastern Yong; Wen Zisheng, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Chief Rectifier of Western Yan; Lu Cao, Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal's Office; Lu Yuanming, Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and Baron of Chengyang; Li Tonggui, Secretariat Gentleman; Xing Ziming, former Secretariat Gentleman; Yuwen Zhongzhi, Secretariat Gentleman; Yuan Zhongjun, former Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works and Baron of Jiankang; Du Bi, Legal Section staff member to the Grand Chancellor; Li Puji, Left Central Military Section Director and Baron of Dingyang; Xin Shu, Initiation Section Director; Yuan Changhe, Sacrificial Section Director; Hu Shirong, former Staff Major of the Qingzhou Agile Cavalry command and Viscount of Anding; Zhao Hongqing, Director of Astronomy and Baron of Luxiang; Hu Fatong, Director of Astronomy; Zhang Zhe, Imperial Rescript Attendant; Cao Weizu, Supernumerary Staff Major; Guo Qing, Assistant Director of Astronomy; Hu Zhonghe, Erudite of Astronomy—and others, some renowned for talent, others inheriting calendrical arts from their families—all joined to elucidate the obscure, reconcile divergent views, and examine past and present records, together completing this calendar. Jia marks the start of the day-cycle, and zi is the true celestial commencement; in establishing a calendar and fixing its epoch, one should begin from these. As fortune now belongs to the Xinghe era, the calendar should take that reign title as its designation—just as the Taichu era name distinguished the Han calendar, and the Jingchu crowned that of Wei. We respectfully submit this in sealed form, requesting that the appropriate offices receive it and put its methods into practice.
4
詔以新曆示齊獻武王田曹參軍信都芳，芳關通曆術，駁業興曰：「今年十二月二十日，新曆歲星在營室十三度，[2]順，疾； 天上歲星在營室十一度。 今月二十日，新曆鎮星在角十一度，留； 天上鎮星在亢四度，留。 今月二十日，新曆太白在斗二十五度，晨見，逆行； 天上太白在斗二十一度，逆行。 便為差殊。」
An edict directed that the new calendar be shown to Xin Du Fang, staff member of the Field Section under the Qi Prince Xianwu. Fang, well versed in calendrical computation, challenged Li Yexing: "On the twentieth day of the twelfth month this year, the new calendar places Jupiter in Encampment at thirteen degrees, [2] in direct motion, swift; yet Jupiter in the sky is in Encampment at eleven degrees. On the twentieth of this month, the new calendar places Saturn in Horn at eleven degrees, stationary; yet Saturn in the sky is in Neck at four degrees, stationary. On the twentieth of this month, the new calendar places Venus in Dipper at twenty-five degrees, visible in the morning, in retrograde; yet Venus in the sky is in Dipper at twenty-one degrees, in retrograde. These are clear discrepancies."
5
業興對曰：
Li Yexing replied:
6
歲星行天，伺候以來八九餘年，恒不及二度。 今新曆加二度。 至於夕伏晨見，纖毫無爽。 今日仰看，如覺二度，及其出沒，還應如術。 鎮星，自造壬子元以來，歲常不及，故加壬子七度，亦知猶不及五度，適欲并加，恐出沒頓校十度、十日，將來永用，不合處多。 太白之行，頓疾頓遲，取其會歸而已。 近十二月二十日，晨見東方，新舊二曆推之，分寸不異。 行星三日，頓校四度。 如此之事，無年不有，至其伏見，還依術法。
Jupiter's course through the heavens, as observed over the past eight or nine years, has consistently lagged by about two degrees. The new calendar therefore adds two degrees. As for its evening setting and morning rising, there is not the slightest discrepancy. Observed today, it may seem off by two degrees, yet when it sets and rises, it will still conform to the computational method. Saturn, since the renzi epoch was established, has year after year lagged behind observation; seven degrees were therefore added to the renzi calendar, yet it still falls short by about five degrees. To add the full amount at once would risk sudden corrections of ten degrees and ten days at rising and setting—creating many discrepancies if the calendar were used indefinitely. Venus moves now swiftly, now slowly; the calendar need only capture its points of conjunction. On the recent twentieth of the twelfth month, when it appeared in the morning in the east, the old and new calendars agreed to the minutest fraction. A planet may shift four degrees in the space of three days. Such variations occur every year; yet when planets set and rise, they still conform to the computational rules.
7
又芳唯嫌十二月二十日星有前却。 業興推步已來，三十餘載，上算千載之日月星辰有見經史者，與涼州趙𢾺、劉義隆廷尉卿何承天、劉駿南徐州從事史祖沖之參校，業興甲子元曆長於三曆一倍。 考洛京已來四十餘歲，五星出沒，歲星、鎮星、太白，業興曆首尾恒中，及有差處，不過一日二日、一度兩度； 三曆之失，動校十日十度。 熒惑一星，伏見體自無常，或不應度。 祖沖之曆多甲子曆十日六度，何承天曆不及三十日二十九度； 今曆還與壬子同，不有加增。 辰星一星，沒多見少，及其見時，與曆無舛，今此亦依壬子元不改。 太白、辰星，唯起夕合為異。 業興以天道高遠，測步難精，五行伏留，推考不易，人目仰窺，未能盡密，但取其見伏大歸，略其中間小謬，如此曆便可行。 若專據所見之驗，不取出沒之效，則曆數之道其幾廢矣。 夫造曆者，節之與朔貫穿於千年之間，閏餘斗分推之於毫釐之內。 必使盈縮得衷，間限數合，周日小分不殊錙銖，陽曆陰曆纖芥無爽，損益之數驗之交會，日所居度考之月蝕，上推下減，先定眾條，然後曆元可求，猶甲子難值。 又雖值甲子，復有差分，如此踳駁，參錯不等。 今曆發元甲子，七率同遵，合璧連珠，其言不失。 法理分明，情謂為可。 如芳所言，信亦不謬。 但一合之裏星度不驗者，至若合終必還。 依術，鎮星前年十二月二十日見差五度，今日差三度； 太白前差四度，今全無差。 以此準之，見伏之驗，尋效可知，將來永用，大體無失。
Moreover, Fang's sole objection concerns the forward and backward discrepancies of the stars on the twentieth of the twelfth month. For more than thirty years since he began his computations, Li Yexing has calculated backward through a millennium of solar, lunar, and planetary positions recorded in the classics and histories, comparing his results with the work of Zhao Fei of Liangzhou, He Chengtian, Minister of Justice under Liu Yilong, and Zu Chongzhi, Attendant Clerk of Southern Xuzhou under Liu Jun. His jiazi-epoch calendar proves twice as accurate as all three of theirs. Examining the past forty-odd years since Luoyang was the capital, the risings and settings of the five planets—Jupiter, Saturn, and Venus—Li Yexing's calendar has consistently matched at both beginning and end; where discrepancies occur, they amount to no more than a day or two, a degree or two; whereas the three rival calendars err by as much as ten days and ten degrees. Mars alone is inherently irregular in its appearances and disappearances, sometimes failing to match the predicted degrees. Zu Chongzhi's calendar runs ten days and six degrees ahead of the jiazi calendar; He Chengtian's falls short by thirty days and twenty-nine degrees; the present calendar still agrees with the renzi system, without further adjustment. Mercury hides often and appears rarely; when it does appear, it matches the calendar without error. The present calendar likewise follows the renzi epoch unchanged. Venus and Mercury differ only in their evening risings and conjunctions. Li Yexing holds that the Heavenly Way is vast and remote, precise measurement difficult, and the hiding and lingering of the five planets hard to compute fully; the naked eye cannot achieve perfect accuracy. One need only capture the broad pattern of their appearances and disappearances, allowing for minor intermediate errors—such a calendar can serve well enough. If one relied solely on momentary observations without considering risings and settings, the art of calendrical computation would be all but abandoned. Calendar-makers must thread solar terms and new moons through a thousand years, and push intercalary remainders and fractional parts to the finest precision. Fullness and contraction must strike the true mean; interval limits and numerical relations must align; fractional parts of the circuit-day must agree to the smallest unit; solar and lunar reckonings must be exact; adjustment figures must be verified at conjunctions; the sun's position must be tested against lunar eclipses. By extrapolating upward and reducing downward, fixing all rules first, the calendar epoch may then be determined—yet as elusive as a perfect jiazi alignment. Even when a jiazi alignment is achieved, fractional discrepancies remain; systems contradict and overlap without ever fully agreeing. The present calendar takes its origin in a jiazi year; the seven computational rates all conform together, like jades joined and pearls strung—its principles hold true. Its principles and methods are clear; we believe it should be adopted. Fang's observations are indeed not without merit. Yet where planetary degrees fail to match within a single conjunction, they will invariably realign by the conjunction's end. By the computational method, Saturn on the twentieth of the twelfth month two years ago showed a five-degree discrepancy; today the discrepancy is three degrees; Venus previously differed by four degrees; now there is no discrepancy at all. Judging by this standard, the verification of risings and settings will soon become clear; for long-term use, the calendar will hold firm in its essentials.
8
芳又云，以去年十二月中算新曆，其鎮星以十二月二十日在角十一度留，天上在亢四度留，是新曆差天五度； 太白、歲星並各有差。 校於壬子舊曆，鎮星差天五度，太白歲星亦各有差，是舊曆差天為多，新曆差天為少。 凡造曆者，皆須積年累日，依法候天，知其疏密，然後審其近者，用作曆術。 不可一月兩月之間，能正是非。 若如熒惑行天七百七十九日，一遲、一疾、一留、一逆、一順、一伏、一見之法，七頭一終； 太白行天五百八十三日，晨夕之法，七頭一終； 歲星行天三百九十八日，七頭一終； 鎮星行天三百七十八日，七頭一終； 辰星行天一百一十五日，晨夕之法，七頭一終。 造曆者必須測知七頭，然後作術。 得七頭者造曆為近，不得頭者其曆甚疏，皆非一二日能知是非。 自五帝三代以來及秦、漢、魏、晉，造曆者皆積年久測，術乃可觀。 其倉卒造者，當時或近，不可久行。 若三四年作者，初雖近天，多載恐失。 今甲子新曆，業興潛構積年，雖有少差，校於壬子元曆，近天者多。 若久而驗天，十年二十年間，比壬子元曆，三星行天，其差為密。
Fang also argued that, calculating from last year's twelfth month, the new calendar places Saturn stationary in Horn at eleven degrees on the twentieth, while in the sky it is stationary in Neck at four degrees—the new calendar thus differing from the heavens by five degrees; Venus and Jupiter each show discrepancies as well. Compared with the old renzi calendar, which also places Saturn five degrees off, along with discrepancies for Venus and Jupiter, the old calendar deviates more from the heavens, the new calendar less. All calendar-makers must accumulate observations over many years, watching the heavens by established methods to learn where computations are loose or tight, then adopt whichever approach proves closest. One cannot settle such questions in the space of a month or two. Consider Mars, which traverses the heavens in seven hundred seventy-nine days through one phase each of slowness, swiftness, station, retrogradation, direct motion, hiding, and appearance—seven phases completing one cycle; Venus, traversing the heavens in five hundred eighty-three days through its morning and evening appearances, seven phases completing one cycle; Jupiter traverses the heavens in three hundred ninety-eight days, seven phases completing one cycle; Saturn traverses the heavens in three hundred seventy-eight days, seven phases completing one cycle; Mercury traverses the heavens in one hundred fifteen days through its morning and evening appearances, seven phases completing one cycle. Calendar-makers must observe and master these seven phases before they can construct their methods. Those who master the seven phases produce calendars that closely match the heavens; those who do not produce very loose ones. In neither case can right and wrong be determined in a day or two. From the Five Emperors and Three Dynasties through Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin, every successful calendar-maker accumulated years of observation before his methods proved reliable. Calendars composed in haste may match the heavens briefly but cannot endure. Even those composed over three or four years, though accurate at first, may drift over the course of many years. The present jiazi calendar, which Li Yexing built upon years of accumulated computation, shows only minor discrepancies; compared with the renzi calendar, it accords more closely with the heavens. If verified over ten or twenty years, the three planets' courses will prove far closer to the heavens than under the renzi calendar.
9
獻武王上言之，詔付外施行。
The Prince Xianwu submitted this report, and an edict ordered the calendar transmitted to the appropriate offices for implementation.

Submergence divisor (mo fa): 88,417. 〈The fractional surplus after completing a sexagenary cycle within one year.〉
30
斗分，四千一百一十七。 〈從斗量周天至此，不成度之分。〉
Dipper-part remainder (dou fen): 4,117. 〈The fractional surplus when the circuit of heaven is measured from the Dipper asterism and does not form whole degrees.〉

虛分，九萬七千八百八十三。 〈經月二十九日外少此，不滿三十日。〉
Deficiency-part constant (xu fen): 97,883. 〈The canonical month is twenty-nine days; subtracting this amount still falls short of thirty days.〉

小分法，二十四。 〈二十四氣除周天分之數也。〉
Minor-parts divisor (xiao fen fa): 24. 〈The divisor used to spread the circuit-of-heaven fraction across the twenty-four solar terms.〉

會數，一百七十三。 〈月一出一入黃道之日數，五月、二十三分月之二十也。〉 [8]
Conjunction number (hui shu): 173. 〈Days for the moon's single passage in and out of the ecliptic: five months plus twenty twenty-thirds of a month.〉 Editorial note 8.

會餘，六萬七千一百一十七。 〈百七十三日[9]外不成日之分。〉
Conjunction remainder (hui yu): 67,117. 〈The fractional surplus after one hundred seventy-three full days[9].〉
36
會通，三千六百一十四萬二千八百七。 〈以日法通百七十三，[10]內會餘之數。〉
Conjunction-communication constant (hui tong): 36,142,807. 〈Day factor times one hundred seventy-three,[10] with the conjunction remainder included.〉
37
會虛，十四萬一千四百一十三。 〈會餘之外不成度之數。〉

周日，二十七。 〈周天用一日月行數除。〉 [11]
Circuit days (zhou ri): 27. 〈Circuit of heaven divided by the moon's daily travel.〉 Editorial note 11.
39
周餘，十一萬五千六百三十一。 〈周天用日外及本處之分數。〉
Circuit remainder (zhou yu): 115,631. 〈The fractional surplus of the circuit of heaven beyond complete days at its base position.〉

Communication-circuit constant (tong zhou): 5,745,941. 〈Day factor times twenty-seven, fractional parts included.〉
41
周虛，九萬二千八百九十九。 〈周餘[12]外不成日之數。〉

Lunar-circuit constant (yue zhou): 225,390. 〈Minor circuit with its full degree-count included.〉

45

47
度餘，十一萬六千五十八半。 〈減半月小餘之外。〉 [13]

48
推月朔弦望術第一
Procedure I: Computing New Moon, First Quarter, Full Moon, and Last Quarter.
49
推積月術曰：置入紀以來盡所求年，減一，以章月乘之，章歲如一，所得為積月，不盡為閏餘。 閏餘三百五十五以上，其年有閏。 餘五百一十五以上，進退在天正十一月前後，以冬至定之。
To compute accumulated months: from the era's opening through the year sought, subtract one, multiply by the rule-months, divide by the rule-years; the quotient is accumulated months and the remainder is the intercalary surplus. When the intercalary remainder reaches 355 or more, the year receives an intercalary month. When the remainder is 515 or higher, adjust placement around the eleventh month of the celestial year, using the winter solstice as the criterion.
50
推積日術曰：以通數乘積月，為朔積分，日法如一，為積日，不盡為小餘。 以六旬去積日，不盡為大餘。 命大餘以紀， 〈今命以甲戌紀。〉 算外，即所求年天正十一月朔日。
To compute accumulated days: multiply accumulated months by the communication number for the new-moon accumulated fraction; divide by the day factor for accumulated days, with the remainder as the small remainder. Cast out full sexagenary cycles from the accumulated days; what remains is the large remainder. Count the large remainder from the era marker, 〈The count is currently taken from the jiaxu era.〉 One day beyond the count gives the new moon of the eleventh month (celestial first month) in the year sought.
51
求次月朔術曰：加大餘二十九、小餘十一萬六百四十七，滿除如上，命以紀，算外，即次月朔日。 其小餘滿虛分九萬七千八百八十三者，其月大； 減者，其月小。
To find the next new moon: add 29 to the large remainder and 110,647 to the small remainder; carry overflow as before, count from the era marker, and one day beyond the tally is the next month's new moon. If the small remainder reaches the deficiency-part constant of 97,883, the month is long; otherwise it is short.
52
求上下弦望術曰：加朔大餘七、小餘七萬九千七百九十四、小分一。 小分滿四，從小餘； 小餘滿日法，從大餘； 大餘滿六十，去之，命以紀，算外，[14]即上弦日。 又加，得望、下弦、後月朔。
To find the first quarter, full moon, and last quarter: add 7 to the new-moon large remainder, 79,794 to the small remainder, and 1 to the minor parts. When minor parts reach four, carry into the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the day factor, carry into the large remainder; when the large remainder reaches sixty, cast it out, count from the era marker, and one day beyond the tally[14] is the first-quarter day. Repeat the addition to get the full moon, last quarter, and the following new moon.
53
推二十四氣閏術第二
Procedure II: The Twenty-Four Solar Terms and Intercalation.
54
推二十四氣術曰：置入紀以來盡所求年，減一，以餘數乘之，蔀法如一，為積沒，不盡為小餘。 以六旬去積沒，不盡為大餘，命以紀，算外，即所求年天正十一月冬至日。
To compute the twenty-four qi: from the era's opening through the year sought, subtract one, multiply by the remainder number, and divide by the obscuration factor; the quotient is accumulated submergence and the remainder is the small remainder. Cast out sexagenary cycles from the accumulated submergence; the remainder is the large remainder; count from the era marker, and one day beyond the tally is the winter solstice of the eleventh month (celestial first month) in the year sought.
55
求次氣術術曰：加大餘十五、小餘三千六百八十四、小分一，小分滿小分法二十四，從小餘； 小餘滿蔀法，從大餘一，命如上，[15]算外，即次氣日。
To find the next solar term: add 15 to the large remainder, 3,684 to the small remainder, and 1 to the minor parts; when minor parts reach the minor-parts divisor of 24, carry into the small remainder; when the small remainder fills the obscuration factor, carry 1 into the large remainder; count as before, and one day beyond the tally[15] is the next solar-term day.
56
推閏術曰：以閏餘減章歲，餘以歲中十二乘之，滿章閏二百七得一，月餘半法以上亦得一月，數起天正十一月，算外，即閏月。 閏月有進退，[16]以無中氣定之。
To determine intercalation: subtract the rule-years from the intercalary remainder, multiply by twelve (mid-year qi), divide by the rule-intercalations of 207; if the month-remainder is at least half the divisor, count another month; start from the eleventh month (celestial first month), and one beyond the tally marks the intercalary month. Intercalary months may be placed forward or back;[16] placement is fixed where no mid-term qi falls.
57
推閏又法術曰：以歲中乘閏餘，如章閏得一，[17]盈章中六千七百四十四，數起冬至，算外，中氣終閏月也。 盈中氣在朔若二日，即前月閏。
Alternate intercalation method: multiply the intercalary remainder by twelve and divide by the rule-intercalations of 207;[17] when the product exceeds the rule-center of 6,744, count from the winter solstice—one beyond the tally marks where the mid-term qi ends and the intercalary month begins. When the excess mid-term qi coincides with the new moon or within two days of it, the intercalary month is placed in the preceding month.
58
冬至十一月中小寒十二月節大寒十二月中立春正月節
Winter Solstice: mid-11th month. Lesser Cold: 12th-month solar node. Greater Cold: mid-12th month. Start of Spring: 1st-month solar node.
59
雨水正月中驁蟄二月節春分二月中清明三月節
Rain Water: mid-1st month. Awakening of Insects: 2nd-month solar node. Spring Equinox: mid-2nd month. Clear and Bright: 3rd-month solar node.
60
穀雨三月中立夏四月節小滿四月中芒種五月節
Grain Rain: mid-3rd month. Start of Summer: 4th-month solar node. Lesser Fullness: mid-4th month. Grain in Ear: 5th-month solar node.
61
夏至五月中小暑六月節大暑六月中立秋七月節
Summer Solstice: mid-5th month. Lesser Heat: 6th-month solar node. Greater Heat: mid-6th month. Start of Autumn: 7th-month solar node.
62
處暑七月中白露八月節秋分八月中寒露九月節
End of Heat: mid-7th month. White Dew: 8th-month solar node. Autumn Equinox: mid-8th month. Cold Dew: 9th-month solar node.
63
霜降九月中立冬十月節小雪十月中大雪十一月節
Frost Descent: mid-9th month. Start of Winter: 10th-month solar node. Lesser Snow: mid-10th month. Greater Snow: 11th-month solar node.
64
推合朔却去度表裏術第三
Procedure III: Syzygy, Crossing Distance, and Inner/Outer Ecliptic Position.
65
推合朔却去交度術曰：置入紀以來朔積分，又以所入紀交會差分并之， 〈甲戌紀交會差分二千六百五十二萬二千六百四十九。〉 以會通去之，所得為積交； 不盡者，以日法約之，為度，不盡者為度餘，即所求年天正十一月朔却去交度及度餘。 甲子紀 〈紀首合朔，日月合璧，交中。〉
To compute syzygy and distance from the lunar node: take the new-moon accumulated fraction from the era's opening and add the conjunction-difference fraction for the era entered, 〈Jiaxu-era conjunction-difference fraction: 26,522,649.〉 subtract the conjunction-communication constant; the quotient is the accumulated crossings; the remainder, divided by the day factor, gives degrees with a degree remainder—this is the crossing distance at the new moon of the eleventh month (celestial first month) in the year sought. Jiazi era-cycle. 〈At the era opening, sun and moon conjoin in syzygy with the node at center.〉
66
甲子紀 〈紀首合朔，日月合璧，交中。〉
Jiazi era-cycle. 〈At the era opening, sun and moon conjoin in syzygy with the node at center.〉
67
甲戌紀 〈紀首合朔，月在日道表。〉 交會差一百二十七度度餘三萬九千三百三十九[18]
Jiaxu era-cycle. 〈At the era opening, the new moon lies north of the ecliptic.〉 Conjunction-difference: 127°; degree remainder 39,339[18].
68
甲申紀 〈紀首合朔，月在日道裏。〉 交會差八十一度度餘一萬一千五百六十一
Jiashen era-cycle. 〈At the era opening, the new moon lies south of the ecliptic.〉 Conjunction-difference: 81°; degree remainder 11,561.
69
甲午紀 〈紀首合朔，月在日道裏。〉 交會差三十四度度餘十九萬二千三百一十三
Jiawu era-cycle. 〈At the era opening, the new moon lies south of the ecliptic.〉 Conjunction-difference: 34°; degree remainder 192,313.
70
甲辰紀 〈紀首合朔，月在日道表。〉 交會差一百六十二度度餘二萬三千一百二十二
Jiachen era-cycle. 〈At the era opening, the new moon lies north of the ecliptic.〉 Conjunction-difference: 162°; degree remainder 23,122.
71
甲寅紀 〈紀首合朔，月在日道表。〉 交會差一百一十五度度餘二十萬三千八百七十四
Jiayin era-cycle. 〈At the era opening, the new moon lies north of the ecliptic.〉 Conjunction-difference: 115°; degree remainder 203,874.
72
求次月却去交度術曰：加度二十九、度餘十一萬六百四十七，度餘滿日法從度，度滿會數去之，亦除其會餘，即次月朔却去交度及度餘。
To find the next month's node distance: add 29 degrees and 110,647 to the degree remainder; carry overflow from the degree remainder through the day factor into degrees; when degrees reach the conjunction number, subtract it and the conjunction remainder—the result is the next new moon's crossing distance and degree remainder.
73
求望却去交度術曰：加度十四、度餘十五萬九千五百八十八半，滿除如上，即望却去交度及度餘。
To find the full moon's node distance: add 14 degrees and 159,588½ to the degree remainder; carry overflow as above—the result is the full moon's crossing distance and degree remainder.
74
推月在日道表裏術曰：置入紀以來朔積分，又以紀交會差分并之，倍會通去之，餘以會通減之，得一減者，為月在日道裏； 無所得者，為月在日道表。
To determine whether the moon lies north or south of the ecliptic: take the new-moon accumulated fraction from the era's opening and add the era's conjunction-difference fraction; cast out double the conjunction-communication constant; subtract the conjunction communication from the remainder; if one subtraction succeeds, the moon is south of the ecliptic; If no subtraction succeeds, the moon is north of the ecliptic.
75
求次月表裏術曰：加次月度及度餘，加表滿會數及會數餘，則在裏； 加裏滿會數及會餘，則在表。
To find the next month's position: add the next month's degrees and degree remainder; if starting from the outer side the conjunction number and its remainder are filled, the moon is on the inner side; If starting from the inner side the conjunction number and remainder are filled, the moon is on the outer side.
76
推交道所在日術曰：以十一月朔却去交度及餘減會數及會餘，會餘若不足減者，減一度，加日法乃減之； 又以十一月朔小餘加之，滿日法從度，餘為度餘，即是天正十一月朔前去交度及餘。 如曆月大小除之，起天正月十一月，不滿月者為入月，算外，交道所在日。 又以歲中乘入月小餘，日法除之，所得命以子，算外，[19]即交道所在辰。 其交在望前者，其月朔則交會，[20]望則月蝕。 交在望後者，其月月蝕，後朔交會。 交正在望者，其月月蝕既，前後朔交會。 交正朔者，日蝕既，前後月望皆月蝕。
To find the day of nodal crossing: subtract the eleventh-month new moon's crossing distance and remainder from the conjunction number and conjunction remainder; if the conjunction remainder is too small, borrow one degree and add the day factor before subtracting; Add the eleventh-month new moon's small remainder; carry overflow through the day factor into degrees, with the remainder as the degree remainder—this is the crossing distance before the new moon of the eleventh month (celestial first month). Divide by the long and short months of the calendar, starting from the eleventh month (celestial first month); the partial month count is the entered month, and one day beyond the tally is the day of nodal crossing. Multiply the entered month's small remainder by mid-year (12), divide by the day factor, count from the zi hour, and one beyond the tally[19] gives the double-hour of nodal crossing. When the node precedes full moon, that month brings a solar eclipse at new moon[20] and a lunar eclipse at full moon. When the node follows full moon, the month has a lunar eclipse first and a solar eclipse at the following new moon. When the node falls exactly at full moon, the month brings a total lunar eclipse, with solar eclipses at the adjacent new moons. When the node falls exactly at new moon, the solar eclipse is total, and both neighboring full moons bring lunar eclipses.
77
求後交月及日術曰：以會數及會餘加前入月算及餘，餘滿日法從日，日如曆月大小除之，起前交月，算外，即後交月及日。 以次放之。
To find the next crossing month and day: add the conjunction number and remainder to the prior entered-month count and remainder; carry remainder overflow through the day factor into days; divide by long and short months starting from the prior crossing month, and one beyond the tally marks the next crossing month and day. Continue in the same manner for successive crossings.
78
推交會起角術曰：其月在外道，先會後交者，虧從東南角起； 先交後會者，虧從西南角起。 其月在內道，先會後交者，虧從西北角起，合交中者，蝕之既。 其月蝕在日之衝，起角亦如之。
To determine the eclipse's starting corner: when the moon is on the outer path and conjunction precedes crossing, the shadow begins at the southeast limb; If crossing precedes conjunction, the shadow begins at the southwest limb. When the moon is on the inner path and conjunction precedes crossing, the shadow begins at the northwest limb; if conjunction and crossing coincide at center, the eclipse is total. For lunar eclipses at opposition, the starting corner follows the same rule.
79
推蝕分多少術曰：其朔望去交度及度餘如入交限數一百五十八度、度餘十一萬六千五十八半以上者，以減會數及會數餘，餘為不蝕度。 若朔望去交度如朔望合數十四度、度餘十五萬九千五百八十八半以下者，即是不蝕度。 [21]皆以減十五，餘為蝕分。 [22]朔望去交度盡者，蝕之既。
To compute eclipse magnitude: if the new-moon or full-moon crossing distance and degree remainder reach the entry-to-crossing limit of 158° with degree remainder 116,058½ or more, subtract the conjunction number and its remainder—the remainder is the non-eclipse arc. If the new-moon or full-moon crossing distance is within the syzygy-conjunction number of 14° with degree remainder 159,588½ or less, that value is the non-eclipse arc. [21]Subtract each from 15; the remainder is the eclipse magnitude. [22]When the crossing distance at new moon or full moon reaches zero, the eclipse is total.
80
推合朔月蝕入遲疾曆盈縮術第四
Procedure IV: Syzygy, Lunar Eclipse, and Entry into the Slow-Fast Sequence with Excess and Shortage.
81
推合朔入遲疾曆術曰：置入紀以來朔積分，又以所入紀遲疾差分并之， 〈甲戌紀遲差分二百三十五萬二千一百九十一。〉 [23]以通周去之，所得為積周； [24]不盡者，以日法約之，為日，不盡者為日餘。 命日，算外，即所求年天正月十一月合朔入曆日。
To compute entry into the slow-fast sequence at syzygy: take the new-moon accumulated fraction from the era's opening and add the slow-fast difference fraction for the era entered, 〈Jiaxu-era slow-difference fraction: 2,352,191.〉 [23]Subtract the communication-cycle constant; the quotient is accumulated cycles; [24]Divide the remainder by the day factor for days, with the leftover as the day remainder. Count the day from the marker; one beyond the tally is the slow-fast sequence day for the new moon of the eleventh month (celestial first month) in the year sought.
82
求次月入曆日術曰：加一日、日餘二十萬三千五百四十六，日蝕滿日法從日，[25]日滿周日及周餘去之，命如上，算外，即次月入曆日。
To find the next month's sequence day: add 1 day and 203,546 to the day remainder; carry overflow through the day factor into days;[25] when days reach the cycle day and cycle remainder, subtract them; count as before, and one beyond the tally is the next month's sequence day.
83

推合朔交會月蝕定大小餘[38]術曰：以入曆日餘乘所入曆下損益率，以小周七千五百一十三除之，所得損益盈縮積分為定積分。 積分盈者，[39]以減本朔望小餘； 縮者，加之。 加之滿日法者，交會加時在後日； 減之，不足減者，減一日，加日法乃減之，交會加時在前日。 月蝕者，隨定大小餘[40]為定日加時。
Procedure for fixing syzygy, crossing, and eclipse remainders[38]: multiply the anomalistic day fraction by the tabulated rate below that entry, divide by the minor circuit of 7,513, and apply the result to the excess-shortage column for the corrected integral. If the integral is in excess,[39] subtract from the base syzygy fractional day; If in shortage, add to it. A carry past the day factor moves the crossing instant to the next civil day; If subtracting underflows, borrow one day, add the day factor, then subtract—the crossing instant falls on the previous day. For lunar eclipses, take the clock time directly from the corrected remainder line[40].
113
推加時術曰：以歲中乘定小餘，日法除之，所得命以子，算外。 朔望加時有餘不盡者，四之，如法得一為少，二為半，三為太。 半又有餘者，三之，如法得一為強，半法以上排成一，不滿半法棄之。 以強并少為少強，并半為半強，并太為太強。 得二強者為少弱，以之并少為半弱，以之并半為太弱，以之并太為一辰弱。 隨所在辰而命之，即其強弱。 日之衝為破，月常在破下蝕。 推日月合朔弦望度術第五[41]推日度術曰：置入紀以來朔積日，以日度法一萬六千八百六十乘之，滿周天去之，餘以日度法約之為度，不盡為餘。 [42]命起牛前十二度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半日所在度及分。
To name the double-hour: multiply the corrected fractional day by mid-year (12), divide by the day factor, count from the zi hour, and read one beyond the tally. For leftover syzygy fractions, quadruple the tail and divide by the day factor for shao, ban, or tai subdivisions. Triple any further tail to reach the qiang step, rounding up at half-divisor. Add qiang units to shao, ban, or tai per the classical clepsydra notation. Two qiang collapse into a weak grade, stepping through the ladder to a full weak double-hour mark. Read the final label against the stem hour to recover the strength grade. The sun's anticenter is the rupture point; the moon eclipses when it stands beneath it. Procedure V: Degrees at Syzygy, Quarters, and Full Moon[41] To compute solar longitude: multiply accumulated new-moon days by the day-degree factor of 16,860, cast out whole circuits of heaven, and divide the remainder by 16,860 for degrees and fractional parts. [42]Count from twelve degrees before Ox, walk through the lodges, and one beyond the tally gives the midnight solar longitude on the eleventh-month (celestial first month) new moon for the year sought.
114
推日度又法，術曰：置周天三百六十五度、斗分四千一百一十七，以冬至去朔日數減一，以減周天度，冬至小餘減斗分； 斗分不足減者，減一度，加日度法乃減之。 命起如上，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半日所在度及分。
Alternate solar-longitude method: take 365° plus 4,117 Dipper parts, subtract (days from new moon to winter solstice minus one) from the degree total and the winter-solstice fractional day from the Dipper parts; If the Dipper parts underflow, borrow one degree and add the day-degree factor before subtracting. Count as above; one beyond the tally gives the midnight solar longitude on the eleventh-month new moon for the year sought.
115
求次月次日日所在度[43]術曰：月大者加度三十，月小者加度二十九，次日者加度一，宿次除之，逕斗除其分。 [44]
To find the next month's or next day's solar longitude[43]: add 30° for a long month, 29° for a short month, or 1° for the next day; walk the lodges and subtract the Dipper-part fraction directly. Editorial note 44.
116
推合朔日月共度術曰：以章歲五百六十二乘朔小餘，以章月六千九百五十一除之，所得為大分，不盡為小分。 以加夜半日度分，分滿日度法從度，命如上，算外，即所求年天正十一月合朔日月共度。
To find syzygy's shared solar-lunar longitude: multiply the new-moon fractional day by 562, divide by 6,951 for the large and small fraction parts. Add this to the midnight solar position, carry overflow through the day-degree factor, count as above, and one beyond the tally is the shared syzygy longitude for the eleventh-month new moon.
117
推合朔日月共度又法，術曰：加度二十九、大分八千九百四十五、小分六千九百一十九，小分滿章月從大分； 大分滿日度法從度，宿次除之，逕斗去其分，算外，即次月合朔日月共度。
Alternate syzygy-longitude method: add 29°, 8,945 large parts, and 6,919 small parts, carrying small-part overflow into large parts at 6,951; Carry large-part overflow into degrees at 16,860, walk the lodges, subtract the Dipper fraction directly, and one beyond the tally is the next month's syzygy longitude.
118
推月度術曰：置入紀以來朔積日，以月周二十二萬五千三百九十乘之，[45]滿周天去之。 餘以日度法約之為度，餘為度分，命起牛前十二度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半月所在度及分。
To compute lunar longitude: multiply accumulated new-moon days by the lunar circuit of 225,390;[45] cast out whole circuits of heaven. Divide the remainder by 16,860 for degrees and parts, count from twelve degrees before Ox through the lodges, and one beyond the tally gives the midnight lunar longitude on the eleventh-month new moon.
119
推月度又法，術曰：以小周乘朔小餘為實，章歲乘日法為法，實如法得一為度； 不滿法者，以章月除之為大分，餘為小分。 所得以減合朔度及度分，算外，即所求年天正十一月朔夜半月所在度及分。
Alternate lunar-longitude method: set dividend = minor circuit × new-moon fractional day, divisor = rule-years × day factor; quotient gives degrees; The remainder divides by 6,951 for large parts, with the tail as small parts. Subtract this from the syzygy longitude; one beyond the tally gives the midnight lunar position on the eleventh-month new moon.
120
求次月月度術[46]曰：月小，加度二十二、分七千三百七十三，月大，加度三十五、分一萬三千五百八十三，分滿日度法從度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即月次月所在度。
Next month's lunar longitude[46]: add 22° 7,373 parts for a short month or 35° 13,583 for a long month, carry through the day-degree factor, walk the lodges, and one beyond the tally marks the result.
121
求次日月度術[47]曰：加度十三、分六千二百一十，分滿日度法從度，除如上，算外，即月次日所在度。
Next day's lunar longitude[47]: add 13° 6,210 parts, carry overflow, remove lodges as above; one beyond the tally is the result.
122
求弦望日所在度術曰：加合朔度七、大分六千四百五十一、小分三千四百六十七、[48]微分二，微分滿四從小分，小分滿章月從大分，大分滿日度法從度，命如上，算外，即上弦日所在度。 又加，得望、[49]下弦、後月合朔。
Solar longitude at first and last quarter: add 7°, 6,451 large parts, 3,467 small parts, and[48] 2 micro-parts to syzygy, carrying at 4, 6,951, and 16,860 respectively; count as above for first-quarter solar longitude. Repeat the addition for full moon,[49] last quarter, and the following syzygy.
123
求弦望月所在度術曰：加合朔度九十八、大分一萬一千六百九十五、小分五千二百二十五、微分一，滿除如上，算外，即上弦日月所在度。 又加，得望、下弦、後月合朔。
Lunar longitude at first and last quarter: add 98°, 11,695 large parts, 5,225 small parts, and 1 micro-part to syzygy, carry as above; one beyond the tally gives first-quarter lunar longitude. Repeat for full moon, last quarter, and the following syzygy.
124

推土王滅沒卦候上朔術第六
Procedure VI: Earth Sovereignty, Extinction/Submergence, Hexagram Seasons, and Superior Syzygy.
138
推土王日術曰：置四立大小餘，各減其大餘十八、小餘四千四百二十、小分十八、微分二，大餘不足減者，加六十乃減之； 小餘不足減者，減一日，加蔀法乃減之； 小分不足減者，減小餘一，加小分法二十四乃減之； 微分不足減者，減小分一，加五，然後皆減之。 命以紀，算外，即四立前土王日。
Earth-sovereignty day method: from each of the four establishing-term remainder lines subtract 18 large, 4,420 small, 18 small-part, and 2 micro-part units, borrowing 60 into the large remainder when needed; If the small remainder underflows, borrow one day and add the obscuration factor before subtracting; If small parts underflow, borrow one from the small remainder and add 24 (the small-part factor) before subtracting; If micro-parts underflow, borrow one small part and add 5 before completing the subtraction. Count from the era marker; one beyond the tally is the Earth-sovereignty day preceding an establishing term.
139
推土王又法，術曰：加冬至大餘二十七、小餘六千六百三十一、小分六、微分三，微分滿五從小分，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘一，命以紀，算外，即季冬土王日。
Alternate Earth-sovereignty method: add 27, 6,631, 6, and 3 to the winter-solstice remainder stack, carrying at 5, 24, and the obscuration factor; count from the era marker for the late-winter Earth-sovereignty day.
140
求次季土王日術曰：加大餘九十一、小餘五千二百四十四、小分六，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，大餘滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，即次季土王日。
Next season's Earth-sovereignty day: add 91, 5,244, and 6, carrying through the small-part and obscuration factors and casting out sexagenary cycles; count from the era marker.
141
推滅沒術曰：因冬至積沒有小餘者，加積沒一，以沒分乘之，以沒法八萬八千四百一十七除之，所得為積日，不盡為沒餘。 六旬去積日，不盡為沒日，命以紀，算外，即所求天正十一月冬至後沒日。
Extinction/submergence method: if the winter-solstice accumulated submergence has a fractional tail, increment the count by one, multiply by the submergence parts, divide by 88,417 for accumulated days and submergence remainder. Cast out sexagenary cycles from the accumulated days; the remainder is the submergence day; count from the era marker for the first submergence after the eleventh-month winter solstice.
142
求次滅術曰：加沒日六十九、沒餘五萬七千二百四十四，沒餘滿沒法從沒日，沒日滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，即次沒日。 餘盡者為滅。
Next extinction day: add 69 days and 57,244 to the submergence remainder, carry through the submergence factor of 88,417, cast out sexagenary cycles, and count from the era marker. A zero remainder marks the extinction day.
143
求次沒術曰：加沒日六十九、沒餘一萬九百一十五、沒分六萬二千二百八十五，沒分滿沒法從沒餘，沒餘滿蔀法從沒日。 命起前沒月，曆月大小除之，不滿月者，即後沒日及沒餘、沒分。 命曰如上，算外，即次沒日。
Next submergence day: add 69 days, 10,915 remainder, and 62,285 parts, carrying through the submergence and obscuration factors. Starting from the prior submergence month, divide by long and short months; the partial month yields the next submergence day, remainder, and parts. Count as above; one beyond the tally is the next submergence day.
144
推四正卦術曰：因冬至大小餘即坎卦用事日，春分即震卦用事日，夏至即離卦用事日，秋分即兌卦用事日。 中孚因坎卦。
Four cardinal hexagram method: the winter-solstice remainder line fixes Kan's governing day; spring equinox fixes Zhen; summer solstice fixes Li; autumn equinox fixes Dui. Zhong Fu derives from the Kan hexagram.
145
求次卦術曰：加坎卦大餘六，小餘一千四百七十三、小分十四、微分四，微分滿五從小分，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，大餘滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，即復卦用事日。
Next hexagram day: add 6, 1,473, 14, and 4 to the Kan line, carrying at 5, 24, and the obscuration factor and casting out sexagenary cycles; count from the era marker for Fu's governing day.
146
十一月，未濟、蹇、頤、中孚、復。
Eleventh month hexagrams: Wei Ji, Jian, Yi, Zhong Fu, and Fu.
147
十二月，屯、謙、睽、升、臨。
Twelfth month: Tun, Qian, Kui, Sheng, and Lin.
148
正月，小過、蒙、益、漸、泰。
First month: Xiao Guo, Meng, Yi, Jian, and Tai.
149
二月，需、隨、晉、解、大壯。
Second month: Xu, Sui, Jin, Xie, and Da Zhuang.
150
三月，豫、訟、蠱、革、夬。
Third month: Yu, Song, Gu, Ge, and Guai.
151
四月，旅、師、比、小畜、乾。
Fourth month: Lü, Shi, Bi, Xiao Xu, and Qian.
152
五月，大有、家人、井、咸、姤。
Fifth month: Da You, Jia Ren, Jing, Xian, and Gou.
153
六月，鼎、豐、渙、履、遯。
Sixth month: Ding, Feng, Huan, Lü, and Dun.
154
七月，恒、節、同人、損、否。
Seventh month: Heng, Jie, Tong Ren, Sun, and Pi.
155
八月，巽、萃、大畜、賁、觀。
Eighth month: Xun, Cui, Da Xu, Bi, and Guan.
156
九月，歸妹、无妄、明夷、困、剝。
Ninth month: Gui Mei, Wu Wang, Ming Yi, Kun, and Bo.
157
十月，艮、既濟、噬嗑、大過、坤。
Tenth month: Gen, Ji Ji, Shi He, Da Guo, and Kun.
158
四正為方伯，中孚為三公，復為天子，屯為諸侯，謙為大夫，睽為九卿，升還從三公，周而復始。
The four cardinal hexagrams map to regional lords; Zhong Fu to the Three Dukes; Fu to the Son of Heaven; Tun to feudal lords; Qian to grand masters; Kui to the nine ministers; Sheng circles back to the Three Dukes—and the cycle repeats.
159
九三應上九，清淨、微溫、陽風； 九三應上六，降赤、决溫、陰雨。 [50]六三應上六，日澤、寒、陰雨； [51]六三應上九，麴塵、決寒、陽風。 諸卦上有陽爻者陽風，上有陰爻者陰雨。
Nine-three responding to upper nine brings clear skies, mild warmth, and yang wind; Nine-three responding to upper six brings reddish haze, abrupt warmth, and yin rain. [50] Six-three responding to upper six brings bright dampness, cold, and overcast rain; [51] Six-three responding to upper nine brings dust haze, piercing cold, and yang wind. For hexagrams generally: an upper yang line predicts yang wind; an upper yin line predicts yin rain.
160
推七十二候術曰：因冬至大小餘即虎始交日，加大餘五、小餘一千二百二十八、微分一，微分滿三從小分，小分滿小分法從小餘，小餘滿蔀法從大餘，大餘滿六十去之，命以紀，算外，依次候日。
Seventy-two seasonal-term method: the winter-solstice remainder stack fixes the "tigers begin mating" day; add 5, 1,228, and 1 micro-part, carrying at 3, 24, and the obscuration factor and casting out sexagenary cycles; count from the era marker for each succeeding term day.
161
冬至虎始交芸始生荔挺生
Winter solstice terms: tigers begin mating; rue sprouts; zhiting sprouts.
162
小寒蚯蚓結麋角解水泉動
Lesser cold: earthworms coiled; elk shed antlers; springs flow.
163
大寒雁北向鵲始巢雉始雊
Greater cold: geese head north; magpies nest; pheasants call.
164
立春鷄始乳東風解凍蟄蟲始振
Start of spring: hens brood; east wind thaws ice; dormant insects awaken.
165
雨水魚上負冰獺祭魚鴻雁來
Rain water: fish surface under ice; otters "sacrifice" fish; swans return.
166
驚蟄始雨水桃始華倉庚鳴
Awakening of insects: rains begin; peaches bloom; orioles sing.
167
春分鷹化為鳩玄鳥至雷始發聲
Spring equinox: hawks turn to cuckoos; swallows arrive; thunder first rolls.
168
清明電始見蟄蟲咸動蟄蟲啟戶
Clear brightness: lightning appears; all dormant insects stir; insects emerge.
169
穀雨桐始華田鼠化為鴽虹始見
Grain rain: paulownia blooms; field mice turn to quail; rainbows appear.
170
立夏萍始生戴勝降桑螻蟈鳴
Start of summer: duckweed sprouts; hoopoes descend on mulberry; mole crickets chirp.
171
小滿蚯蚓出王瓜生苦菜秀
Lesser fullness: earthworms surface; serpent gourd grows; bitter greens flourish.
172
芒種靡草死小暑至螗蜋生
Bearded grain: tender grasses die; lesser heat arrives; mantises hatch.
173
夏至鵙始鳴反舌無聲鹿角解
Summer solstice: shrike-cicadas call; mockingbirds fall silent; deer shed antlers.
174
小暑蟬始鳴半夏生木槿榮
Lesser heat: cicadas sing; pinellia grows; hibiscus blooms.
175
大暑溫風至蟋蟀居壁鷹乃學習
Greater heat: warm winds blow; crickets move to walls; fledgling hawks practice flight.
176
立秋腐草化為螢土潤溽暑涼風至
Start of autumn: rotting grass becomes fireflies; earth damp with humid heat; cool winds blow.
177
處暑白露降寒蟬鳴鷹祭鳥
End of heat: white dew falls; cold cicadas cry; hawks hunt birds.
178
白露天地始肅暴風至鴻雁來
White dew: heaven and earth turn austere; storms rise; swans return.
179
秋分玄鳥歸羣鳥養羞雷始收聲
Autumn equinox: swallows depart; birds hoard food; thunder fades.
180
寒露蟄蟲附戶殺氣浸盛陽氣日衰
Cold dew: insects shelter by doors; killing qi gathers; yang qi wanes day by day.
181
霜降水始涸鴻雁來賓雀入大水化為蛤
Frost descends: waters shrink; swans arrive as guests; sparrows enter the waters and turn to clams.
182
立冬菊有黃華豺祭獸水始冰
Start of winter: chrysanthemums bloom yellow; jackals hunt game; waters begin to ice.
183
小雪地始凍雉入大水為蜃虹藏不見
Lesser snow: earth freezes; pheasants enter the waters as shen-clams; rainbows vanish.
184
大雪冰益壯地始坼鶡旦不鳴[52]
Greater snow: ice hardens; earth cracks; crossbills fall silent at dawn[52].
185
推上朔術曰：置入紀以來盡所求年，減一，以六律乘之，以六旬去之，不盡者命以甲子，算外，[53]即上朔日。
Superior syzygy method: take years since era entry for the year sought, subtract 1, multiply by 6, cast out sexagenary cycles, count from jiazi; one beyond the tally[53] is the superior syzygy day.
186
推五星見伏術第七
Procedure VII: Five Stars, Appearance and Occultation.
187
上元甲子以來至今大魏興和二年，歲在庚申，積二十九萬三千九百九十七算。
From the upper origin in a jiazi year to the present—Great Wei's Xinghe year 2, a gengshen year—the accumulated count is 293,997.
188
木精曰歲星，其數六百七十二萬三千八百八十八。
Wood's essence is Jupiter; its divisor is 6,723,888.
189
火精曰熒惑，其數一千三百一十四萬九千八十三。
Fire's essence is Mars; its divisor is 13,149,083.
190
土精曰鎮星，其數六百三十七萬四千六十一。
Earth's essence is Saturn; its divisor is 6,374,061.
191
金精曰太白，其數九百八十四萬三千八百八十二。
Metal's essence is Venus; its divisor is 9,843,882.
192
水精曰辰星，其數一百九十五萬三千七百一十六。 [54]
Water's essence is Mercury; its divisor is 1,953,716. Editorial note 54.
193
推五星術曰：置上元以來盡所求年，減一，以周天乘之，為五星之實； 各以其數為法，除之，所得為積合，不盡為合餘。 以合餘減法，餘為入歲度分。 以日度法約之，所得即所求年天正十一月冬至後晨夕合度算及度餘。 其金、水，以一合日數及合餘減合度算及度餘，得一者為晨，無所得者為夕； 若度餘不足減者，減合度算一，加日度法乃減之。 命起牛前十二度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即所求年天正十一月冬至後晨夕合度及度餘。
Five-star method: take years from the upper origin to the year sought, subtract 1, multiply by the celestial circuit for the five-star dividend; divide each by its planet's divisor for accumulated conjunction and conjunction remainder. Subtract the conjunction remainder from the divisor for the year's degree-fraction. Reduce by the day-degree factor for the morning/evening conjunction degree count and remainder after the eleventh-month winter solstice. For Venus and Mercury, subtract one conjunction-day count and remainder from the degree tally; a result of 1 means morning, 0 means evening; If the degree remainder underflows, borrow 1 from the degree tally and add the day-degree factor before subtracting. Count from 12° before Ox, walk the lodges; the partial lodge yields the morning/evening conjunction longitude and remainder after the eleventh-month winter solstice.
194
徑推五星術曰：置上元以來盡所求年，減一，如法算之。 合度餘滿日度法，加合度算一，合度算滿合終日數去之。 亦以合終日餘減合度餘，[55]若不足減者，減合度算一，加周虛。 [56]所得即所求年天正十一月冬至後晨夕合度算及度餘。 其求金水及命度，[57]皆如上法。
Direct five-star method: take years from the upper origin to the year sought, subtract 1, and compute by each planet's divisor. Carry conjunction degree-remainder overflow into the degree tally; when the tally fills the planet's total conjunction-day count, cast it out. Subtract the total conjunction-day remainder from the degree remainder;[55] if underflow occurs, borrow 1 from the degree tally and add cycle void. [56] The result is the morning/evening conjunction degree count and remainder after the eleventh-month winter solstice. Finding Venus, Mercury, and their assigned longitudes[57] all follow the method above.
195
求星合月及日術曰：置冬至去朔日數，減一，加合度算。 冬至小餘以加合度餘，合度餘滿日度法去之，加合度算一。 合度算變成合日算，合度餘為日餘，命日起天正十一月，如曆月大小除之，不滿月者，算外，即星合月及日。 有閏以閏計之。
Star conjunction month and day: set days from winter solstice to new moon, subtract 1, add the conjunction-degree tally. Add the winter-solstice fractional day to the degree remainder, carry overflow into the degree tally. Convert the degree tally to a day tally and the degree remainder to a day remainder; count from the eleventh month through long and short months for the conjunction month and day. When an intercalary month occurs, include it in the count.
196
求後合月及日術曰：以合終日數及合終日餘加前入月算及餘，餘滿日度法從日，[58]如曆月大小除之，起前合月，算外，即後合月及日。 其金、水以一合日數及合日餘加之，[59]加夕得晨，加晨得夕也。
Next conjunction month and day: add total conjunction-day count and remainder to the prior month entry tally, carry through the day-degree factor,[58] walk long and short months from the prior conjunction month. For Venus and Mercury, add one conjunction-day count and remainder;[59] adding to evening gives morning, and to morning gives evening.
197
求後合度術曰：以行星度餘加前合度及度餘，度餘滿日度法從度，命起前合度，宿次除之，不滿宿者，算外，即後合度餘。 逕斗除其分，其分四千一百一十七。
Later conjunction longitude: add the planet's motion degree-fraction to the prior conjunction position, carry through the day-degree factor, walk the lodges from the prior conjunction for the next longitude and remainder. Subtract the Dipper-part fraction directly: 4,117 parts.
198
歲星：合終日數三百九十八，合終日餘一萬二千六百八，周虛三千二百五十二，行星三十三度，度餘八千四百九十一。 [60]
Jupiter: total conjunction days 398, remainder 12,608, cycle void 3,252, motion 33°, degree remainder 8,491. Editorial note 60.

歲星：晨與日合，在日後伏，十六日、日餘六千八百四，行星二度、度餘一萬三千一百七十五。 晨見東方，順，疾，日行五十八分之十一，五十八日行十一度。 順，遲，日行九分，五十八日行九度而留。 不行，二十五日而旋。 逆，日行七分之一，八十四日退十二度。 復留，二十五日。 復順，遲，日行九分，五十八日行九度。 復順，疾，日行十一分，五十八日行十一度。 在日前，夕伏西方，順，十六日、日餘六千八百四，行星二度、度餘一萬三千一百七十六，而與日合。
Jupiter: conjunction at dawn, occultation behind the sun—16 days and remainder 6,804, motion 2° with remainder 13,175. Morning visibility in the east, prograde and fast: 11/58° per day, 11° in 58 days. Prograde, slow: 9/58° per day, 9° in 58 days, then stationary. Stationary 25 days, then retrograde reversal. Retrograde: 1/7° per day, retreating 12° in 84 days. Stationary again for 25 days. Prograde again, slow: 9/58° per day, 9° in 58 days. Prograde again, fast: 11/58° per day, 11° in 58 days. West of the sun, evening occultation in the west, prograde—16 days and remainder 6,804, motion 2° with remainder 13,176, then conjunction with the sun.

熒惑：合終日數七百七十九，合終日餘一萬五千一百四十三，周虛一千七百一十七，行星四十九度，度餘六千九百九。
Mars: total conjunction days 779, remainder 15,143, cycle void 1,717, motion 49°, degree remainder 6,999.

熒惑：晨與日合，在日後伏，七十一日、日餘一萬六千一，行星五十五度、度餘一萬三千九百四十三。 晨見東方，順，疾，日行二十三分之十四，一百八十四日行一百一十二度。 順，遲，日行十二分，九十二日行四十八度而留。 [61]不行，十一日而旋。 逆，日行六十二分之十七，六十二日退十七度。 復留，十一日。 復順，遲，日行十二分，九十二日行四十八度。 復順，疾，日行十四分，一百八十四日行一百一十二度。 在日前，夕伏西方，順，七十一日、日餘一萬六千二，行星五十五度、[62]度餘一萬三千九百四十三，而與日合。
Mars: dawn conjunction, occultation behind the sun—71 days and remainder 16,001, motion 55° with remainder 13,943. Morning visibility in the east, prograde and fast: 14/23° per day, 112° in 184 days. Prograde, slow: 12/92° per day, 48° in 92 days, then stationary. [61] Stationary 11 days, then retrograde reversal. Retrograde: 17/62° per day, retreating 17° in 62 days. 鎮星：合終日數三百七十八，合終日餘九百八十一，周虛一萬五千八百七十九，行星十二度，度餘一萬三千七百二十四。

鎮星：晨與日合，在日後伏，十八日、日餘四百九十，行星二度、度餘六千八百六十二。 晨見東方，順，日行十二分之一，八十四日行七度而留。 不行，三十六日而旋。 逆，日行十七分之一，一百二日退六度。 復留，三十六日。 復順，日行十二分之一，八十四日行七度。 在日前，夕伏西方，順，十八日、日餘四百九十一，行星二度、度餘六千八百六十二而與日合。

太白：合終日數五百八十三，合終日餘一萬四千五百二，周虛二千三百五十八，行星二百九十一度， 〈亦曰一合日數。〉 度餘一萬五千六百八十一。 [63] 〈亦曰一合日數。〉
Venus: total conjunction days 583, remainder 14,502, cycle void 2,358, motion 291°, 〈Also termed the one-conjunction day count.〉 degree remainder 15,681. Editorial note 63. 〈Also termed the one-conjunction day count.〉

太白：夕與日合，在日前伏，四十一日、日餘一萬五千六百八十一，行星五十一度、度餘一萬五千六百八十一。 夕見西方，順，疾，日行一度十三分之三，九十一日行一百一十二度。 [64]順，遲，日行一度十三分之二，九十一日行一百五度。 [65]順，大遲，日行十五分之十一，[66]四十五日行三十三度而留。 不行，八日而旋。 逆，日行三分之二，九日退六度。 在日前，夕伏西方，伏六日，退四度，而與日晨合。

太白：晨與日合，在日後，伏六日，退四度。 晨見東方，逆，日行三分之二，九日退六度而留。 不行，八日。 順，日行十五分之十一，四十五日行三十三度。 順，疾，日行一度十三分之二，九十一日行一百五度。 順，大疾，日行一度十三分之三，[67]九十一日行一百一十二度。 在日後，晨伏東方，順，四十一日、日餘一萬五千六百八十一，行星五十一度、度餘一萬五千六百八十一，而與日夕合。
Venus: dawn conjunction, occultation behind the sun—6 days, retreat 4°. Morning visibility in the east, retrograde: 2/3° per day, retreating 6° in 9 days, then stationary. Stationary 8 days. 辰星：合終日數一百一十五，合終日餘一萬四千八百一十六，[68]周虛二千四十四，行星五十七度， 〈亦曰一合日數。〉 度餘一萬五千八百三十八。 [69] 〈亦曰一合日數。〉
Mercury: total conjunction days 115, remainder 14,816, [68] cycle void 2,044, motion 57°, 〈Also termed the one-conjunction day count.〉 degree remainder 15,838. Editorial note 69. 〈Also termed the one-conjunction day count.〉

辰星：夕與日合，在日前伏，十七日、日餘一萬五千八百三十八，行星三十四度、度餘一萬五千八百三十八。 [70]夕見西方，順，疾，日行一度三分之一，十八日行二十四度。 順，遲，日行七分之五，七日行五度而留。 不行，四日。 在日前，夕伏西方，逆，十一日退六度，而與日晨合。

[70] Evening visibility in the west, prograde and fast: 1 + 1/3° per day, 24° in 18 days. Prograde, slow: 5/7° per day, 5° in 7 days, then stationary. Stationary 4 days. West of the sun, evening occultation in the west, retrograde—11 days, retreat 6°, then morning conjunction with the sun.

辰星：晨與日合，在日後伏，十一日，退六度。 晨見東方而留，不行，四日。 順，遲，日行七分之五，七日行五度。 順，疾，日行一度三分之一，十八日行二十四度。 在日後，晨伏東方，順，十七日、日餘一萬五千八百三十八，行星三十四度、度餘一萬五千八百三十八，[71]而與日夕合。
Mercury: dawn conjunction, occultation behind the sun—11 days, retreat 6°. Morning visibility in the east, then stationary—no motion for 4 days. Prograde, slow: 5/7° per day, 5° in 7 days. Prograde, fast: 1 + 1/3° per day, 24° in 18 days. East of the sun, morning occultation in the east, prograde—17 days and remainder 15,838, motion 34° with remainder 15,838, [71] then evening conjunction with the sun.
210
五星曆步術曰：以術法伏日度及餘加星合日度及餘，餘滿日度法一萬六千八百六十得一，從全命之如前，[72]得星見日度及餘。 以星行分母乘見度分，日度法如一得一分，不盡半法以上亦得一，以加所行分，分滿其母得一度。 逆順母不同，以當行之母乘故分，故母如一，為當行分。 留者承前，逆則減之，伏不書度，[73]除斗分，以行母為率，分有損益，前後相御。 [74]
Five-star ephemeris steps: add occultation day-degree and remainder to conjunction day-degree and remainder; carry at the day-degree factor 16,860; assign as before[72] for the star's appearance day-degree and remainder. Multiply visible degree-fraction by the motion denominator; take one part per day-degree factor, rounding up at half the factor; add to motion parts and carry when the denominator fills for whole degrees. When retrograde and direct denominators differ, convert former parts to current motion parts by cross-multiplication. Stationary phases inherit the prior position; retrograde subtracts; occultation omits degrees;[73] subtract the Dipper fraction, using the motion denominator as rate, with fractional adjustments linked between successive steps. Editorial note 74.
211
求五星行所在度術曰：以行分子乘行日數，分母除之，所得即星行所在度。
Planet's current longitude: multiply the motion numerator by elapsed motion days and divide by the denominator.
212
校勘記
Collation Notes
213
置差令朔「令朔」不可解，疑「令」乃「合」之訛。
"Set discrepancies to align the new moon": "align new moon" is unintelligible; "令" is probably a corruption of "合" (conjunction).
214
新曆歲星在營室十三度諸本「新曆」下脫「歲星」兩字，依下文鎮星、太白例補。
"New calendar, Year Star in Encampment Room at 13°": all editions omit 歲星 after 新曆; restored following the Saturn and Venus entries below.
215
十蔀成紀諸本「十」作「千」。 按蔀法一萬六千八百六十，十蔀成十六萬八千六百，正為一紀之數。 「千」顯誤，今改正。
"Ten obscurations form an era-cycle": all editions read 千 for 十. The obscuration factor is 16,860; ten obscurations yield 168,600—the count of one era-cycle. "Thousand" is clearly wrong; corrected here.
216
十二分度法諸本「十」作「小」。 按以十二除度法一萬六千八百六十，得一千四百五，乃為一氣時法之數。 「小」係形近致誤，今改正。
"Twelve-part degree method": all editions read 小 for 十. Dividing the degree factor 16,860 by 12 yields 1,405—the qi-term time factor. "Small" is a graphic corruption; corrected here.
217
二十九章十一年減閏餘一一萬六百七十八年減一閏月諸本「閏餘一，一」作「閏餘二」，「六百」作「一百」，「減」下有「右」字。 按興和曆一章歲等於古法 (十九年一章) 之二十九章加十一年，而閏餘減一； 積十九章歲，即一萬六百七十八年則減一閏月。 傳本將「閏餘一，一萬」之兩「一」字誤并成「二」字，「六百」誤為「一百」，又衍「右」字，今俱改正。
"Twenty-nine rules and eleven years reduce the intercalation remainder by one; 10,678 years reduce one intercalary month": all editions read 閏餘二 for 閏餘一，一, 一百 for 六百, and add 右 after 減. By the Xinghe calendar, one rule-year equals that of the ancient method (nineteen years per rule) — twenty-nine rules plus eleven years, with the intercalation remainder reduced by one; after nineteen accumulated rule-years—that is, 10,678 years—one intercalary month is subtracted. The transmitted text merged the two 一 in 閏餘一，一萬 into 二, changed 六百 to 一百, and added a spurious 右; all corrected here.
218
閏月數諸本「閏」訛「間」，今依文義改。
"Intercalary month count": all editions read 間 for 閏; corrected per context.
219
內分五萬七千二百四十四諸本「二百四十四」作「一百八十四」。 按以沒法八萬八千四百一十七除沒分六百一十五萬八千一十七，得經沒六十九、分五萬二百四十四。 數字顯誤，今改正。
"Inner parts 57,244": all editions read 一百八十四 for 二百四十四. Dividing the extinction part 6,158,017 by the extinction factor 88,417 yields 69 extinction cycles and remainder 50,244. The numeral is clearly wrong; corrected here.
220
五月二十三分月之二十也諸本「五月」作「周髀六」。 按會數為五月二十三分月之二十的整日數，「周髀六」三字當衍，又脫「五月」兩字。 今改正。
"May, twenty-three parts of the month's twenty": all editions read 周髀六 for 五月. The conjunction number is the whole-day count of "May, 23/20 of a month"; 周髀六 is an interpolation and 五月 is missing. Corrected here.
221
百七十三日諸本「三」作「二」。 按此數即上會數，「二」字訛，今改正。
"173 days": all editions read 二 for 三. This is the conjunction number above; 二 is wrong; corrected here.
222
百七十三諸本「三」作「二」。 按此數亦即上會數，「二」字訛，今改正。
"173": all editions read 二 for 三. This is likewise the conjunction number above; 二 is wrong; corrected here.
223
周天用一日月行數除諸本「日」上脫「一」字，「數」下脫「除」字。 按周日為小周 (即一日月行數) 除周天所得之整數。 原文脫漏，今補。
"Circuit of heaven divided by one day's moon-motion count": all editions omit 一 before 日 and 除 after 數. The circuit remainder is the lesser circuit (that is, one day's moon-motion count) the whole number obtained by dividing the circuit of heaven. The original text is defective; supplied here.
224
周餘諸本「周」訛「用」，今依文義改正。
"Circuit remainder": all editions read 用 for 周; corrected per context.
225
減半月小餘之外按入交限數為會通減通數之半，除以日法，即得一百五十八度。 其餘數為十一萬六千五十八半。 此注或由錯簡，致與正文迥無關係，依術當作「一百五十八度外不成度之數」。
"Beyond subtracting half the lunation's small remainder": the entry-into-crossing limit is half of (conjunction common minus common number), divided by the day factor, yielding 158°. The remaining number is 116,058.5. This note may be a misbound interpolation unrelated to the main text; per the method it should read "the fractional degrees outside 158°."
226
命以紀算外諸本「算」下脫「外」字，今依文義補。
"Assign beyond the era tally": all editions omit 外 after 算; supplied per context.
227
命如上諸本「上」訛「止」，今依文義改正。
"Assign as above": all editions read 止 for 上; corrected per context.
228
閏月有進退諸本「退」訛「即」，今依文義改正。
"Intercalary months have advance and retreat": all editions read 即 for 退; corrected per context.
229
如章閏得一諸本「如」訛「加」，今依文義改正。
"When the rule intercalation yields one": all editions read 加 for 如; corrected per context.
230
度餘三萬九千三百三十九諸本「三十九」作「四十九」。 按甲戌紀交會差二千六百五十二萬二千六百四十九除以日法二十萬八千五百三十，得交會差一百二十七度、度餘三萬九千三百三十九。 「四十」乃「三十」之訛，今改正。
"Degree remainder 39,339": all editions read 四十九 for 三十九. Dividing the jiaxu-era conjunction discrepancy 26,522,649 by the day factor 208,530 yields a conjunction discrepancy of 127° with remainder 39,339. "Forty" is a corruption of "thirty"; corrected here.
231
算外諸本「算」下脫「外」字，今依文義補。
"Beyond the tally": all editions omit 外 after 算; supplied per context.
232
其月朔則交會諸本「會」訛「道」，今依文義改正。
"That month's new moon then crosses in conjunction": all editions read 道 for 會; corrected per context.
233
即是不蝕度諸本「蝕」訛「餘」，今依文義改正。
"That is the non-eclipse degree": all editions read 餘 for 蝕; corrected per context.
234
餘為蝕分諸本「為」下衍「餘」字，今依文義刪。
"The remainder is the eclipse fraction": all editions add a spurious 餘 after 為; deleted per context.
235
甲戌紀遲差分二百三十五萬二千一百九十一諸本「二百」作「二日」，「二千」作「三千」。 按以一紀月數二百八萬五千三百乘通數六百一十五萬八千一十七，以通周五百七十四萬五千九百四十一去之，得甲戌紀遲差分二百三十五萬二千一百九十一。 知「日」乃「百」之訛，「三千」乃「二千」之訛，今改正。
"Jiaxu-era slow-discrepancy parts 2,352,191": all editions read 二日 for 二百 and 三千 for 二千. Multiplying one era-cycle's month count 2,085,300 by the common number 6,158,017 and subtracting the common circuit 5,745,941 yields jiaxu-era slow-discrepancy parts 2,352,191. Recognizing 日 as a corruption of 百 and 三千 of 二千; corrected here.
236
所得為積周諸本「為積周」訛「日餘周」，今依正光曆例改正。
"What is obtained is accumulated circuits": all editions read 日餘周 for 為積周; corrected per the Zhengguang calendar.
237
日蝕滿日法從日諸本「日法從日」誤倒作「日從日法」，今依文義乙正。
"When the eclipse fills the day factor, carry to days": all editions invert 日法從日 as 日從日法; reordered per context.
238
月行遲疾度及分諸本「分」訛「合」，今依文義改正。
"Moon's slow and fast motion degrees and parts": all editions read 合 for 分; corrected per context.
239
十四度 〈三百三十四分〉 諸本「三十四分」作「三十十四分」，衍一「十」字。 按本表各項數字，今依下列方法加以校算： (一) 月行遲疾度及分：以月日平行分七千五百一十三 (即小周) 加減本日損益率 (損減、益加) ，以章歲五百六十二約之為度，餘為分。 (二) 損益率：以各日月實行度分化為分，減以月日平行分七千五百一十三即得。 (三) 盈縮并率：將本日前各日損益率累加得之。 (四) 盈縮積分：盈縮并率乘日法二十萬八千五百三十，約以小周七千五百一十三，即得。 以下至校勘記[三七]，逕指出傳本譌誤所在，校改理由不再贅述。
14°. 〈334 parts.〉 All editions read 三十十四分 for 三十四分—one spurious 十. The figures in this table are now rechecked by the following methods: (1) Moon slow/fast degrees and parts: using the moon-sun mean motion parts 7,513 (that is, the lesser circuit) add or subtract this day's correction rate (subtract for 損, add for 益) , divide by the rule-years constant of 562 to obtain degrees; the remainder is the fractional parts. (2) Correction rate: convert each tabulated sun-moon actual motion value into parts, subtract the mean motion parts of 7,513, and the result is the rate. (3) Combined excess/shortage rate: sum all correction rates from preceding days through the current day. (4) Accumulated excess/shortage parts: multiply the combined rate by the day factor of 208,530, then divide by the lesser circuit of 7,513. From here through collation note [37], each entry simply marks the error in the transmitted text; detailed arguments for the emendations are omitted.
240
盈七百五十七諸本「十」下脫「七」字，今據校算補。
"Excess 757": all editions omit 七 after 十; supplied per recalculation.
241
二百六十一分諸本「二百」下衍「四十」兩字，今據校算刪。
"261 parts": all editions add spurious 四十 after 二百; deleted per recalculation.
242
益六百一十六諸本「十六」訛「十七」，今據校算改正。
"Increase 616": all editions read 十七 for 十六; corrected per recalculation.
243
盈一千四百四十六諸本「四十六」訛「三十六」，今據校算改正。
"Excess 1,446": all editions read 三十六 for 四十六; corrected per recalculation.
244
四百六十八分諸本「六十八分」訛「八十六分」，今據校算乙正。
"468 parts": all editions read 八十六分 for 六十八分; characters reordered per recalculation.
245
二百六十七分諸本「二百」訛「三百」，今據校算改正。
"267 parts": all editions read 三百 for 二百; corrected per recalculation.
246
益六百四十六諸本「四十六」訛「三十六」，今據校算改正。
"Increase 646": all editions read 三十六 for 四十六; corrected per recalculation.
247
三百二十四分諸本「三百」訛「二百」，今據校算改正。
"324 parts": all editions read 二百 for 三百; corrected per recalculation.
248
十三度諸本「十三」訛「十二」，今據校算改正。
"13°": all editions read 十二 for 十三; corrected per recalculation.
249
三百四十六分諸本「四十六」訛「三十六」，今據校算改正。
"346 parts": all editions read 三十六 for 四十六; corrected per recalculation.
250
定大小餘諸本「餘」訛「蝕」，今依文義改正。
"Fixed large and small remainders": all editions read 蝕 for 餘; corrected per context.
251
積分盈者諸本「盈」訛「盛」，今依文義改正。
"When accumulated parts are in excess": all editions read 盛 for 盈; corrected per context.
252
隨定大小餘諸本「小」下衍「蝕」字，今依文義刪。
"Following, fix large and small remainders": all editions add a spurious 蝕 after 小; deleted per context.
253
推日月合朔弦望度術第五諸本「度」下脫「術」字，今依本術前後各標題例補。
"Method V for computing sun-moon syzygy, quarter, and full-moon positions": all editions omit 術 after 度; supplied per the standard heading format used elsewhere in this chapter.
254
不盡為餘諸本「餘」上脫「不盡為」三字，今依文義補。
"What does not exhaust becomes remainder": all editions omit 不盡為 before 餘; supplied per context.
255
求次月次日日所在度諸本「次月次日」作「日次月次」。 按依術文，先求次月日所在度，次求次日日所在度，傳本誤倒，今乙正。
"Seek the degree where the sun is on the next month and next day": all editions read 日次月次 for 次月次日. Per the procedure, one first finds the sun's position for the following month, then for the following day; the transmitted text reverses this order; reordered here.
256
逕斗除其分諸本「逕」訛「遙」，今依文義改正。
"Directly use the Dipper to divide off its parts": all editions read 遙 for 逕; corrected per context.
257
以月周二十二萬五千三百九十乘之諸本「周」上脫「月」字，今依文義補。
"Multiply by the moon circuit of 225,390": all editions omit 月 before 周; supplied per context.
258
求次月月度術諸本「次月」訛「月次」，今據上正光曆例乙正。
"Method for the next month's lunar position": all editions read 月次 for 次月; reordered per the Zhengguang calendar above.
259
求次日月度術諸本「次日月度」訛「月次日度」，今據上正光曆乙正。
"Method for the next day's lunar position": all editions read 月次日度 for 次日月度; reordered per the Zhengguang calendar above.
260
小分三千四百六十七諸本「七」作「一」。 按以四除一經月度數：度二十九、大分八千九百四十五、小分六千九百一十九，得上弦度數：度七、大分六千四百五十一、小分三千四百六十七、微分二。 小分尾數「一」字乃「七」之訛，今改正。
"Small parts 3,467": all editions read 一 for 七. Dividing one anomalistic month (29°, major parts 8,945, small parts 6,919) by four yields the first-quarter position: 7°, major parts 6,451, small parts 3,467, micro parts 2. The final small-part digit 一 is a corruption of 七; corrected here.
261
又加得望諸本「加」作「如」。 殿本考證云「如字當作加」，說是，今改正。
"Again add to obtain full moon": all editions read 如 for 加. The Palace Edition notes that 如 should read 加; this is correct; corrected here.
262
降赤決溫陰雨「降赤」，本志上正光曆作「絳赤」，疑作「絳赤」是。
"Deep crimson, sultry warmth, overcast rain": for 降赤, the Zhengguang calendar in this monograph reads 絳赤 (dark crimson); 絳赤 is probably the correct reading.
263
日澤寒陰雨「日澤、寒、陰雨」，本志上正光曆作「白濁、微寒、陰雨」，疑此「日澤」乃「白濁」之訛，又脫「微」字。
"Sun-marsh, cold, overcast rain": the Zhengguang calendar reads 白濁、微寒、陰雨; 日澤 is probably a corruption of 白濁, and 微 is also missing.
264
鶡旦不鳴諸本「鳴」上無「不」字。 按本志上正光曆作「鶡旦不鳴」。 據禮月令作「鶡旦不鳴」，呂氏春秋仲冬作「鶡鴠不鳴」，淮南子時則篇作「鳱鴠不鳴」，則以有「不」字為是。 今據補。
"The crossbill does not sing at dawn": all editions omit 不 before 鳴. The Zhengguang calendar in this monograph reads 鶡旦不鳴. The Book of Rites Monthly Ordinances reads 鶡旦不鳴; Lüshi Chunqiu (mid-winter) reads 鶡鴠不鳴; Huainanzi Seasonal Regulations reads 鳱鴠不鳴—confirming that 不 belongs in the text. Supplied accordingly.
265
算外諸本「外」訛「上」，今據正光曆推上朔法改正。
"Beyond the tally": all editions read 上 for 外; corrected per the Zhengguang calendar's prior-syzygy procedure.
266
其數一百九十五萬三千七百一十六諸本「十六」作「十七」。 按辰星合終日數一百一十五乘以度法一萬六千八百六十，并以合終日餘一萬四千八百一十六 (此數末位尾數「六」原文誤作「八」，參閱校勘記[六八]) ，得一百九十五萬三千七百一十六。 尾數「十七」乃「十六」之訛，今改正。
"The number is 1,953,716": all editions read 十七 for 十六. Mercury's total conjunction days (115) times the degree factor (16,860), plus the total conjunction day remainder (14,816) (The final digit 六 was corrupted to 八 in the source text; see collation note [68].) , yields 1,953,716. The final digits 十七 are a corruption of 十六; corrected here.
267
減合度餘諸本「度」下脫「餘」字，今依文義補。
"Subtract the conjunction degree remainder": all editions omit 餘 after 度; supplied per context.
268
加周虛諸本於「加周虛」下衍「積年盡」三字，今依文義刪。
"Add circuit emptiness": all editions add spurious 積年盡 after 加周虛; deleted per context.
269
其求金水及命度諸本「水」上奪「金」字。 按上推五星術於求得冬至後晨夕合度算及度餘後，述求金、水冬至後晨夕合度及度餘術。 則此處不當單求水一星，今補。
"In seeking Venus, Mercury, and apogee degrees": all editions omit 金 before 水. In the five-planet procedure above, after computing morning/evening conjunction positions and remainders from the winter solstice, the text then gives the method for Venus and Mercury morning/evening conjunctions. So this passage should not treat Mercury alone; 金 is supplied here.
270
餘滿日度法從日諸本「從」訛「後」，「從日」下又衍「一日」兩字，今依文義刪改。
"When the remainder fills the day-degree factor, carry to days": all editions read 後 for 從, and add spurious 一日 after 從日; deleted and emended per context.
271
以一合日數及合日餘加之諸本「以一合日數及合日數」誤倒作「以合日數及一合日餘」，今依文義乙正。
"Add the one-conjunction day count and conjunction day remainder": all editions invert the phrase as 以合日數及一合日餘; reordered per context.
272
度餘八千四百九十一諸本「八千」作「九千」。 按歲星數六百七十二萬二千八百八十八減以周天六百一十五萬八千一十七，餘除以度法一萬六千八百六十，得行星三十三度、度餘八千四百九十一。 知「九千」乃「八千」之訛，今改正。
"Degree remainder 8,491": all editions read 九千 for 八千. Jupiter's constant (6,722,888) minus the circuit of heaven (6,158,017), divided by the degree factor (16,860), yields 33° with remainder 8,491. Thus 九千 is a corruption of 八千; corrected here.
273
九十二日行四十八度而留諸本「二」作「一」。 按熒惑日行二十三分之十二分，則九十二日行四十八度，不當為九十一日，今改正。
"In 92 days it travels 48° and stations": all editions read 一 for 二. Mars moves 12/23 of a degree per day; over 92 days that is 48°, not 91 days; corrected here.
274
行星五十五度諸本「十」下無「五」字。 按熒惑在日前後，伏行星度當相等，上文在日後伏作「行星五十五度」； 依其伏、行、留、逆之總行度計，當以此數為是，傳本脫「五」字，今據補。
"Planetary motion 55°": all editions omit 五 after 十. Before and after superior conjunction, Mars's hidden motion should be equal; the passage after conjunction already gives 行星五十五度; and the total motion through occultation, direct motion, station, and retrograde confirms this figure; the transmitted text drops 五; supplied here.
275
度餘一萬五千六百八十一諸本「度餘一萬」誤倒作「度一餘萬」，今依文義乙正。
"Degree remainder 15,681": all editions invert 度餘一萬 as 度一餘萬; reordered per context.
276
九十一日行一百一十二度諸本「一百」作「二百」。 按太白日行一度十三分之三，乘以九十一，則得一百一十二度，「二」字訛，今改正。
"In 91 days it travels 112°": all editions read 二百 for 一百. Venus moves 3/13 of a degree per day; over 91 days that is 112°; 二 is erroneous; corrected here.
277
九十一日行一百五度諸本「五」上脫「一百」。 按太白日行一度十三分之二，乘以九十一日，應行一百五度； 下太白在日后，以同速運行九十一日，正作「一百五度」。 今據補。
"In 91 days it travels 105°": all editions omit 一百 before 五. Venus moves 2/13 of a degree per day; over 91 days that yields 105°; and the passage below for Venus after the sun, at the same speed over 91 days, correctly reads 一百五度. Supplied accordingly.
278
順大遲日行十五分之十一諸本「遲」作「疾」。 按太白日行十五分之十一為最遲，不當為大疾，今改正。
"Direct, greatly slow, daily motion 11/15": all editions read 疾 for 遲. Venus's rate of 11/15 is its slowest direct motion; it cannot be labeled "greatly fast"; corrected here.
279
日行一度十三分之三諸本下「三」字作「二」。 按以九十一除一百一十二度，得日行一度十三分之三。 「二」乃「三」之訛，今改正。
"Daily motion 1° 3/13": all editions read 二 for the final 三. Dividing 112° by 91 yields a daily rate of 1° 3/13. 二 is a corruption of 三; corrected here.
280
合終日餘一萬四千八百一十六諸本「十六」作「十八」。 按以度法一萬六千八百六十除辰星數一百九十五萬三千七百一十七，得合終日數一百一十五，合終日餘一萬四千八百一十六； 而以周虛二千四十四減度法一萬六千八百六十，所得日餘亦同，足證末位尾數當為「六」。 今改正。
"Total conjunction day remainder 14,816": all editions read 十八 for 十六. Dividing Mercury's constant 1,953,717 by the degree factor (16,860) yields total conjunction days of 115 and remainder 14,816; and subtracting the circuit emptiness (2,044) from the degree factor (16,860) yields the same day remainder—confirming the final digit should be 六. Corrected here.
281
度餘一萬五千八百三十八諸本「三十八」作「四十八」。 按以二除辰星合終日數一百一十五、日餘一萬四千八百一十六，得行星度五十七、度餘一萬五千八百三十八。 知「四十八」乃「三十八」之訛，今改正。
"Degree remainder 15,838": all editions read 四十八 for 三十八. Dividing Mercury's total conjunction days (115) and remainder (14,816) by two yields 57° with remainder 15,838. Thus 四十八 is a corruption of 三十八; corrected here.
282
日餘一萬五千八百三十八行星三十四度度餘一萬五千八百三十八諸本日餘末兩位數「三十八」作「四十八」，其下並脫「行星三十四度、度餘一萬五千八百三十八」數字。 按辰星在日前后之伏行留逆互為對稱。 下文在日後晨伏東方項下作：「十七日、日餘一萬五千八百三十八」，其下有「行星三十四度、度餘一萬五千八百三十八」十七字。 其在日前後伏行留逆之總日數各為五十七日、日餘一萬五千八百三十八，總行度各為五十七度、度餘一萬五千八百三十八，知此處脫文。 今改補。
"Day remainder 15,838, planetary motion 34°, degree remainder 15,838": all editions read 四十八 for the final digits of the day remainder and omit the following 行星三十四度、度餘一萬五千八百三十八. Mercury's occultation, direct motion, station, and retrograde before and after the sun are symmetrical. The corresponding passage below (morning occultation in the east after the sun) reads: "17 days, day remainder 15,838," followed by 行星三十四度、度餘一萬五千八百三十八. Before and after the sun, total days of occultation, motion, station, and retrograde are each 57 days with remainder 15,838, and total motion is each 57° with remainder 15,838—indicating lacuna here. Emended and supplied here.
283
度餘一萬五千八百三十八諸本「三十八」訛「四十八」，今改正。 詳上條校記。
"Degree remainder 15,838": all editions read 四十八 for 三十八; corrected here. See the preceding collation note.
284
從全命之如前諸本「全」誤作「令」，今依文義改正。
"Proceed from the full apogee as before": all editions read 令 for 全; corrected per context.
285
伏不書度諸本「書」作「盡」。 按李銳四分術注謂「伏不書度」云「謂不以所在宿度書於術」。 李說是，於此亦然，「盡」當作「書」，今據改。
"When hidden, do not record degrees": all editions read 盡 for 書. Li Rui's commentary on the Quarter-Remainder Method glosses 伏不書度 as "do not enter the star-lodge position in the procedure." Li's reading is correct here as well; 盡 should read 書; emended accordingly.
286
前後相御諸本「相御」下衍「十四」兩字，今據晉書卷一七律曆志中載景初曆五星曆步術文刪。
"Front and back mutually connected": all editions add spurious 十四 after 相御; deleted per the Jingchu five-planet procedure in Jin Shu, Treatise on Music and Calendars, juan 7.
